The '''Grunt family''' is a military family from ''[[The Sims 2]]'' and returns in ''[[The Sims 4]]'', available in the [[The Sims 4 Gallery|Gallery]].<ref>[https://www.ea.com/games/the-sims/the-sims-4/gallery/item/8ezu8juxEemA3X5qYTkq6g The Grunt Family by Maxis]</ref> They live in [[Strangetown]], a neighborhood that comes with the base game. [[General Buzz Grunt|General Buzz]] is the father of three sons named [[Tank Grunt|Tank]], [[Ripp Grunt|Ripp]], and [[Buck Grunt|Buck]]. Tank wants to be more like his father, while Ripp just wants some romance, and little Buck is just left out. His wife, [[Lyla Grunt|Lyla]], divorced him and was later electrocuted under mysterious circumstances. She is buried in the [[Specter family]] graveyard.

General Buzz and Tank have a grudge against the [[Curious family]] for being so strange, and the [[Smith family]] due to them being aliens, but Ripp and Buck have positive relationships with [[Johnny Smith|Johnny]] and [[Jill Smith]], respectively.

The family picture to the right can give a pretty good image of the family members' personalities, and why they clash so much: Tank and Buzz are clearly domineering and tough. Ripp just seems lazy, while Buck appears to be more sensitive, thoughtful, and studious. Out of all their deceased relatives, only Lyla and [[Mary Melons]] can be resurrected.

When the family is first played, it is a Sunday morning. The game will provide a scripted notification for the player to have Tank search for a job, which is rigged to always be the military career:

''"Young Tank really wants his father's approval. Will finding a good job and working hard finally win Tank his father's respect? Use the computer to start the job search."''

{{FamilyPage
|etymology = 
*'''Grunt''':  A low, short guttural sound made by an animal or a person. It is also an informal term for a low-ranking soldier.
*'''Buzz''': May refer to the "buzz cut" hairstyle, which many military recruits receive when they enter training.
*'''Lyla''': A name of Hebrew and Arabic origin meaning "night".
*'''Tank''': The name of an armored fighting vehicle used in the military.
*'''Ripp''': Shortened form of the German and Dutch name Rippert. It means "power and famous".
*'''Buck''': The male of various animals. Possibly a reference to the informal military term "the lowest of a particular rank". A possible reference to Buck being the youngest son.
*'''Chip''' (Gen. Buzz's father): A common short form of the names Charles and Christopher. 
*'''Missy''' (Gen. Buzz's mother): Could either mean a young girl or is possibly the short form of Melissa. 
*'''Mike Steel''' (Missy's father): The short form of Michael, from the Hebrew phrase "who is like god". Steel refers to the metal alloy steel, known for being a strong, durable material. 
*'''Mary Melons''' (Missy's mother): Has multiple meanings, such as "beloved", "bitter", and "rebelliousness". Melons refer to the fruit melon.
*'''Rock''' (Chip's father): Possibly referring to him being like a rock. It is also a last name that is now used as a first name, referring to the topography for someone living near a rock or an oak.
*'''Wanda''' (Chip's mother): A name of Polish origin, possibly derived from the tribal name for the Wends, which is a historical name for Slavs living near Germanic settlement areas.
*'''A.P. Vandermorgan''' (Lyla's father): A possible reference to the American businessman, Cornelius Vander Starr, who was the founder of the business C.V. Starr. Vandermorgan is most likely a last name of Dutch origin. As "Vander" is most likely a Dutch prefix meaning "of the". While Morgan is a name of Welsh and Breton origin, possibly meaning "sea chief", "sea protector", "sea defender", or "sailor/captain".
*'''Jacqueline''' (Lyla's mother): Comes from French, as the feminine form of Jacques, which originated from Jacob, a Hebrew name meaning "may God protect" or "supplanter".

The '''Beaker family''' is a pre-made family that first appeared in [[Strangetown]] from ''[[The Sims 2]]'' and returned in the downloadable neighborhood of [[Aurora Skies]] from ''[[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]]'' and [[Oasis Landing]] from ''[[The Sims 3: Into the Future]]''.

==Biography ==

=== The Sims 2===
The family from ''[[The Sims 2]]'' consists of married couple [[Loki Beaker|Loki]] and [[Circe Beaker|Circe]], and their test guinea pig, [[Nervous Subject]]. They reside in a large mansion on a hill, complete with a cell-like room in the basement for Nervous, and several suspicious-looking machines, which are mostly [[Career rewards|career]] and [[Aspiration reward (The Sims 2)|aspiration rewards]]. Their address is [[1 Tesla Court]], located near the alien crash site. The Beakers have a longstanding rivalry with the [[Curious family]], probably stemming from the fact that [[Vidcund Curious]] was Circe's first flame. On Loki's side of the family, he and his sister are possibly of Scandinavian, most likely Icelandic, descent, judging from the last name of their maternal grandparents, Halfdanarson, and the first names of all their relatives. Circe may be of Greek descent on her father's side of the family.

Upon loading the lot for the first time, the game will direct the player to get Circe to work in a good mood in order to receive her desired promotion, at which she will most likely always succeed.  

''"Circe wants a big promotion! Get her to work in a good mood, and maybe her efforts will pay off!"''

The [[welcome wagon]] will also arrive, implying that the Beakers have just moved into 1 Tesla Court; however, the images found in the household's album suggest otherwise. 

In earlier development stages of the game, the Beaker family was seemingly meant to introduce the player to the [[sims:Cut_content#Big_Boss_Scenario|Big Boss Scenario]], according to an [https://tcrf.net/The_Sims_2_(Windows)/Early_Strings#Strangetown early string] found in the game files, before it ultimately got scrapped entirely. Additionally, Circe's friend [[Meredith Lillard (Strangetown)|Meredith Lillard]] has some unused Big Boss text strings leftover in her character file.

=== The Sims 3===
In ''[[The Sims 3]]'', the family returns in the downloadable neighborhood of [[Aurora Skies]]. [[Bjorn Beaker|Bjorn]], [[Gundrun Beaker|Gundrun]], Loki, and [[Erin Singles|Erin]] are present. According to their bio, their family is implied to live for "friendly science in a friendly society", strongly contrasting the ethically questionable experiments Loki and his wife Circe conduct on Nervous Subject in ''The Sims 2''.

The family also returned to [[Oasis Landing]]. Loki's genetically engineered children, [[Atom Beaker|Atom]] and [[Ceres Beaker|Ceres]], were transported into the future through a scientific experiment.

=== The Sims 4 ===
An official [[Maxis]] [https://www.ea.com/games/the-sims/the-sims-4/gallery/item/DvqXGEaNEemHKnldy2Ruvw recreation] of ''The Sims 2'' Beaker family was uploaded to the ''[[The Sims 4]]'' [[Gallery]] on March 19, 2019, marking the 19th anniversary of ''[[The Sims]]''. In addition to Loki, Circe, and Nervous, the household also features young Atom and Ceres as Loki's children.

The '''Newbie family''' is a pre-made family that appears in most games in [[The Sims (series)|''The Sims'' series]]. The family name is a pun of "newbie", which means a newcomer or novice. This is a reference since they are commonly used as a tutorial family, most notably in ''The Sims''. The family name is also a placeholder name in most console games when players create a Sim, which is usually Pat or Chris Newbie.

==The Sims 3==
The Newbie family lives in [[Riverview]], one of the [[World|worlds]] available for purchase from [[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]]. It consists of a married couple, [[Robert Newbie|Robert]] and [[Mags Newbie|Mags]], and their son, [[Bob Newbie|Bob]]. The Newbies are new in town, and they don't appear as a tutorial family in this neighborhood.

The Newbies' house is small but rather fashionably decorated, though they only have §2,000 in their household funds. They also have a swimming pool and an expensive car. This will usually mean that when the first lot of household bills arrives on the second in-game day, before Robert and Mags have been to work for the first time, the bills will take up over half of their small savings. This apparent overspending may explain why the Newbie family is not very well off in future games, despite seeming to be in a good financial situation at the moment.

== The Sims 3 (Wii) ==
The Newbies can be found on the Wii version of ''[[The Sims 3 (Wii)|The Sims 3]]'', living in the town of [[Vista Beach]] in Habitable Pylon at 5010 Lemon St. The family consists of a married couple, [[Tammy Newbie|Tammy]] and [[Nathan Newbie|Nathan]], and their two [[Child|children]], [[Edna Newbie|Edna]] and [[Eddie Newbie|Eddie]]. In the beta version of ''The Sims 3'' for Wii, a placeholder Sim named Chris Newbie will be the first thing you seen when entering [[Create a Sim|CAS]]. Similar to the [[Goth family|Goths]] of Vista Beach, their relation to the Newbie family is unknown, neither is it ever officially stated that they have any connection to them.

== The Sims==
The Newbie family, consisting of Bob and [[Betty Newbie]] {{Nee|Simovich}}, lives at [[7 Sim Lane]] in ''The Sims''. In this game, the Newbies are used as a tutorial family. This tutorial must be completed before the Newbie family can be played.

==The Sims 2 ==
In ''[[The Sims 2]]'', the Newbies are no longer playable, as they are already deceased. Their only daughter, [[Brandi Broke]], and their grandchildren [[Dustin Broke|Dustin]], [[Beau Broke|Beau]], and the [[unborn baby Broke]] are descendants of the Newbies and are now known as the [[Broke family]] in [[Pleasantview]]. Bob and Betty only appear in Brandi's [[family tree]].

The Newbie family appears in [[The Sims 2 (console)|''The Sims 2'' for console]]. They also appear in [[The Sims 2 Pets (console)|''The Sims 2 Pets'' for console]] as a tutorial family as well. The playable members are Bob and Betty, as well as [[Buddy Newbie]] in ''Pets'' for console. Their appearances, however, are very different than the previous games. Both of their skin tones are darker than those in the other games.

==The Sims 4==
As of February 15, 2019, an official recreation by [[Maxis]] of ''The Sims 2: Pets'' console version of the Newbie family in ''[[The Sims 4]]'' can be found in the [[Gallery]].<ref>[https://www.ea.com/games/the-sims/the-sims-4/gallery/item/i7gNazFzEemOZHldy2Ruvw The Newbie Family by Maxis]</ref>

If the player does not have ''[[The Sims 4: Cats & Dogs]]'', Buddy is absent from the family, as this expansion pack is needed in order to have dogs. The family description also has the part "with their dog Buddy" removed. Other pack-specific content is changed as well if the player lacks the required packs.

When you have this much money, you're your own worst enemy. |members = [[Malcolm Landgraab]], [[Mom Landgraab]], [[Mimi Landgraab]], [[Dudley Landgraab]] |generations = 2 |lot = |funds = |game = The Sims 4 |play = Gallery |neighbor = }} The '''Landgraab family''' is a wealthy family dynasty that resides in [[Bluewater Village]] in ''[[The Sims 2]]'', [[Sunset Valley]] in ''[[The Sims 3]]'', and [[Oasis Springs]] in ''[[The Sims 4]]''. The family name is occasionally spelled "'''Landgrabb'''", mostly in ''[[The Sims]]'' and ''[[The Sims Bustin' Out (console)|The Sims Bustin' Out]]'' for console. Which spelling is used depends on which game or expansion pack introduced the object or place, and the Sim that used it. [[Landgraab Industries]] is featured prominently in both building names in ''[[w:c:simcity:SimCity 3000|SimCity 3000]]'' and brand names for objects in ''The Sims''. Most of the family's wealth appears to come from property and real estate (In ''SimCity 3000'', they are associated more with residential property building, a role which resurfaced in ''Bustin' Out'' when most of the town seemed to fail to pay their rent.) In other Sims games, they are more associated with commercial property, giving the Landgraab name a literal meaning of "grabbing the land". ==History== ===Origins=== The Landgraab fortune, or at least a sizable part of it, presumably dates back to a historical figure named Gregory Landgraab, who does not appear in any known version of the Landgraab family tree. If ''[[The Sims 2: Seasons]]'' is installed, a chance card for the [[adventurer]] career reads as follows:
Around the turn of the century, Gregory Landgraab, a humble school teacher, suddenly came into a great deal of money and became one of the wealthiest landowners around. This was never explained, though many theories suggest foul play and the Ministry of Adventure has tasked (name) with solving the case, once and for all. After a great deal of research, (name) believes one of two people will have the answers he/she needs: Spencer Oswald, the Landgraab's accountant or the local fortune teller, the [[gypsy]]. Who should (name) bring in for questioning?
The mentioned Gregory shares the same name as [[Gregory Landgraab|Gregory]] of [[Oasis Landing]]. This could be a coincidence, as it's highly unlikely that they're the same person; alternatively, the Gregory from Oasis Landing could be named for the original Gregory. ===Demetrius and Dacian Landegraab=== In ''[[The Sims Medieval: Pirates & Nobles]]'', a family under the name of Landegraab appears. They own the city of Tredony, known as one of the richest cities in the [[kingdom]]. There are only two family members, a father and son, [[Demetrius Landegraab|Demetrius]] and [[Dacian Landegraab|Dacian]]. Tredony and a neighboring city, Aarbyville, are at war, and the player has the choice of choosing sides in the war. If Demetrius and Dacian were direct ancestors of the Landgraab family, they would be the oldest known family members. ===Admiral Landgraab=== In ''The Sims'', ''[[The Sims: Hot Date]],'' and ''[[The Sims: Vacation]]'', [[Admiral Landgraab]] is mentioned as another historical figure with an extensive background. Wren's Fens National Park on [[Vacation Island]] is described as one of his first colonial acquisitions. An Admiral Landgraab nutcracker can be bought on Vacation Island, and some items refer to him. His portrait, which is available in [[buy mode]], includes a short bio. Admiral Landgraab's first name is not given, and his relationship to [[Malcolm Landgraab IV|Malcolm IV]] of Bluewater Village and the Landgraabs of Sunset Valley is unknown. He likely lived after Gregory, as that would give the family time to gain prestige, but this is not confirmed. However, Admiral Landgraab might also be Gregory himself instead. His exploits are much further elaborated on in ''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures]]''. Despite being his descendants, the Landgraab family has no easier time navigating his chateau in [[Champs Les Sims]]. They also get no bonuses for doing so. ===The Sims 3=== In ''[[The Sims 3]]'', the Landgraabs are seen living in one of three mansions (the other two being the Goth mansion and the Alto mansion) and are already very wealthy. [[Nancy Landgraab|Nancy]] is a Landgraab by birth, born to [[Chester Landgraab|Chester]] and [[Queenie Landgraab|Queenie]], and followed the family legacy by becoming vice president of the business district. At one point before the game, she married a modest, artistic doctor named [[Geoffrey Landgraab|Geoffrey]], who took his wife's name for its privileged status. They had a son named Malcolm, a smart child whom Nancy is attempting to make a proper heir. However, it is stated that Nancy is too busy with work and publicity to dote on Malcolm, so although he is friends with his parents, he has a better relationship with his father than his mother, and constantly dreams of being a doctor every time his father gets a promotion. It is unknown how they are related to the Landgraabs from ''The Sims 2'', yet they share the same old-money theme and prestige. They live in a large home and have §75,000 in household funds. It is also mentioned several times in ''The Sims 3'' that Nancy's family helped start the town. It says in the family bio that "Nancy's family more or less founded the town", while the description of Sunset Valley states that "before Pleasantview, the town was founded by the Goths and built up by the Landgraabs". They have a business feud with the [[Alto Family|Altos]], and are enemies with them, though young Malcolm and [[Holly Alto (Sunset Valley)|Holly Alto]] do not quarrel with each other. The Landgraab family is "old money", so they likely inherited their money from the earlier generation of Landgraabs that founded the town. However, it does not specify who exactly founded the town. It is possible that Admiral Landgraab, being the earliest mention of the Landgraab family from ''[[The Sims]]'', is the town founder. However, he is not listed in the Landgraab family tree for ''The Sims 3'', so [[Kermit Landgraab|Kermit]] and/or [[Kitty Landgraab|Kitty]] would be primarily who built up the town since [[Goth Family|the Goths]] founded [[Sunset Valley]] and [[Pleasantview]]. [[The Sims 3: World Adventures|The Sims 3: World Adventures]] also contains a possible hint that the Landgraabs' influence extends beyond [[SimNation]]. During the Egyptian adventure "Local Intel", the player is asked to question residents of [[Al Simhara|Al Simhara]] about [[MorcuCorp]]. One resident responds:
"I wish MorcuCorp would leave! It's all a big conspiracy you see, between their secret leaders, the Landgraabs, and those Illsiminati guys! They are taking over the world!"
This dialogue explicitly associates the Landgraab family with [[MorcuCorp]] and the mysterious [[Illsiminati]], adding layers to the family international business and political connections. However, as the statement is presented as a conspiracy theory voiced by an individual resident, it is unclear whether the connection is factual within the game's lore or merely an in-universe rumor. ====Magnus Landgraab==== If a Sim is level 10 in the thief branch of the criminal career, they can get a random event mentioning Magnus Landgraab. The event reads:
(Sim Name) was scoping out another job when he/she noticed that Magnus Landgraab was getting a delivery of expensive solid platinum induction coils for some nefarious purpose. Using his/her incredible skills he/she managed to snag one of these coils for free money. Magnus will never notice, especially since his plans never work anyways.
From the description of the event, it can be concluded that Magnus is a thief or evil inventor whose "plans never work". In addition, if a Sim works in a [[law enforcement]] career at level 10, another random event might occur, where the Sim will foil Magnus' plan to take over a small nation. [[File:OpportunityLandgraab.png|250px|The law enforcement event which mentions Magnus Landgraab.]] ==== Francois Landgraab ==== Francois Landgraab is a food critic mentioned in a random event for the [[Culinary]] career. He is a famous and feared food critic.
What a scare. The famous critic, Francois Landgraab came into the restaurant and demanded a meal fit for a king. Everyone ran but (Sim Name), who did his/her best and came up with a tasty new twist to an old favorite. The Beast has been appeased.
===The Sims 3 (console)=== In [[The Sims 3 (console)|''The Sims 3'' for PS3/XBOX360]], [[Malcolm Landgraab (The Sims 3)|Malcolm]] is an adult who has grown up and moved to [[Moonlight Bay]]. He has a wife named [[Hannelore Landgraab|Hannelore]] and a son named [[Adrien Landgraab|Adrien]]. ===The Sims (console) and The Sims: Bustin' Out=== In ''[[The Sims (console)|The Sims for PS2, XBOX, and Gamecube]]'', a character named Malcolm Landgraab is the richest man around, who gives the main character real estate opportunities (fixing up each house they live in to sell at a higher price), and later marries [[Mom Landgraab|their mom]]. His children are [[Dudley Landgraab|Dudley]] and [[Mimi Landgraab|Mimi]], both slackers, party animals, and heirs to his vast fortune. In the sequel, ''[[The Sims Bustin' Out (console)|The Sims Bustin' Out]]'', Malcolm and Mom divorce, and he flies into a rage of repossessing everyone's money and goods before the player stops him. Depending on the player's choices, a senator named Malcolm Landgraab can be eliminated as part of a government conspiracy. In the final stage, Mom chases Malcolm out of his mansion. Maxis uploaded an updated version of the characters in The Sims 4 Gallery, finally confirming the Malcolm Landgraab from these games is the same one from The Sims 3 and The Sims 4, son of Nancy and Geoffrey Landgraab. ===The Sims 3: Pets (Nintendo DS)=== In [[The Sims 3: Pets (Nintendo 3DS)]], [[Juliette Landgraab]] lives in [[Port Abel]] in a regular suburban home with her chihuahua [[Romeo Landgraab]].
The Landgraabs were quick to buy up the prime real-estate in Port Abel. They had a luxurious mansion built on this lot.
[[File:Landgraabs port abel.JPG|center|thumb]] ===The Sims 2=== In ''[[The Sims 2]]'', the Landgraabs are mentioned in the first expansion pack, ''[[The Sims 2: University|University]]''. One of the dorms at [[Sim State University]] is named "Landgraab House", and the secret society there is known as the [[Landgraab Society]]. The connections, whether past or present, between the family and Sim State are not mentioned. In ''[[The Sims 2: Open for Business|Open for Business]]'', [[Malcolm Landgraab IV|Malcolm IV]] is introduced as a bachelor in a very large mansion in [[Bluewater Village]]. His family tree reveals exactly who his parents and grandparents are, but it only dates back to Malcolm II and not Malcolm I. Malcolm IV owns Club Dante and the Electronics Supercenter in Bluewater Village. While he is rich, most of his money is tied up in the house and its furnishings. The neighborhood view shows that his initial net worth is around §197,000, but he starts with around §28,000 in funds. ===The Sims 3 Store=== In [[Lunar Lakes]], the Landgraab household consists of elder scientist [[Christina Landgraab|Christina]] and her three clone children; [[Chris Landgraab|Chris]], an [[Ambitious (The Sims 3)|ambitious]] and [[Snob (The Sims 3)|snobby]] young adult who wants to be a [[Politics|politician]], and twin teenagers [[Chrissie Landgraab|Chrissie]] and [[Christa Landgraab|Christa]], who both want to be independent and do not wish to follow Christina's structured plans for them. While they live in a large and expensive house, they start with §10,000 in funds. All household members have the [[Genius (The Sims 3)|genius]] and [[heavy sleeper]] traits. Also in Lunar Lakes is a deceased adult Sim, [[Posie Landgraab]]. Whether or not she is related to Christina and her children is unknown. In [[Midnight Hollow]], the Landgraab household consists of just [[Todd Landgraab|Todd]]. He is a rich gentleman who, with [[Entrepreneurs household|his roommates]], aspires to be an entrepreneur based on pressure to make something of himself, but it's unknown whether he is related to the Landgraab family or only shares their surname. ===The Sims 3: Into the Future=== The Landgraab family reappeared in [[Oasis Landing]]. The household consists of [[Gregory Landgraab|Gregory]], [[Cheryl Landgraab|Cheryl]], [[Timothy Landgraab|Timothy]], [[Lara Landgraab|Lara]], and the family [[Plumbot]], [[Model U]]. Unlike the Landgraab families from other worlds, the family is unplayable at the start of the game. Gregory shares the same name as Gregory Landgraab, who is mentioned in the [[chance card]] of the [[adventurer]] career in ''[[The Sims 2: Seasons|Seasons]]'', as stated [[Landgraab family#Origins|above]]. ===The Sims 4=== The Landgraab family appears in ''[[The Sims 4]]'', which takes place in an alternate universe from previous games in the series. The family can be found living in a mansion in [[Oasis Springs]], and is made up of the same three family members who appeared in ''The Sims 3'': Geoffrey, Nancy, and Malcolm. Like their former incarnations, Geoffrey and Nancy are adults; Malcolm, however, has been aged up from a child to a teen. One notable difference between the universes is that while Malcolm in ''The Sims 3'' had the [[good]] trait, Malcolm in ''The Sims 4'' is [[evil]], and Nancy, who was portrayed as a snobbish but overall kind businesswoman in the former, is a career [[criminal]] in the latter. Meanwhile, though Geoffrey's personality remains almost unchanged, his career has changed from medicine to [[secret agent]], something which the family bio implies will create tension in his marriage to Nancy, once it emerges that they operate on opposite sides of the law. A fourth member of the Landgraab family, [[Johnny Zest]], appears in Oasis Springs in ''The Sims 4'', though he neither lives with the rest of the family nor shares their last name. Johnny's bio explains that the family disowned him when he announced his intention to become a professional [[Entertainment|comedian]], and that subsequently, he now uses his stage name all the time. Johnny's relation to the Landgraabs was initially not specified, but as of [[The Sims 4/Patch 193|patch 193]], he is set as Nancy and Geoffrey's son, and Malcolm's older brother. SimValley Map.png The Last Simoleon promo.jpg The last simoleon.JPG ===The Sims: Bustin' Out (console)=== [[File:Malcolm's Mansion HD.png|thumb]][[File:Malcolm's Mansion Sims Bustin out.JPG|thumb|Malcolm's Mansion in-game map view]] '''Malcolm's Mansion''' is a [[residential lot]] in SimValley in ''The Sims Bustin' Out''. It is the home of Malcolm Landgraab. Players can only reach this lot in story mode by reaching level 9 of their chosen career. It is the most expensive lot in the game leading to large bills — up to several thousand [[Simoleons]] every few days.
Malcolm's Mansion is the ultimate destination for your Sim, slightly less impressive than an ascent into Heaven. The only problem is that you'll have to get through Malcolm to move in here. Paradise always has a price.
{{clr}} ===The Sims 2: Open for Business=== [[File:74 Gondola Way (Original).png|thumb]] In ''The Sims 2: Open for Business'', Malcolm IV lives alone in a huge mansion on [[74 Gondola Way]] in [[Bluewater Village]]. The house is large by Sims standards and features a large office and balcony, a hot tub, and an indoor swimming pool. Oddly, the house has no television, even though Malcolm owns an electronics store. There is also a strange, empty shed to the left of the house. Its size and placement are just right for it to be a garage, with the addition of a driveway, a garage door, and, of course, a car. Also worth noting is that there are several blank white walls on the upstairs portion of the house, and while they are painted an "off-white", the player might prefer to revamp the second floor to match the rest of the house's interior. The house has very expensive furniture and many of its new mission-style furnishings that are featured in ''Open For Business''. It also has hedges and a few rose bushes to the left and right of the entrance, and some trees and bushes in the back. Malcolm would do well to hire a [[gardener]] or [[butler]]{{vgversion|TS2:AL}}, especially if ''[[The Sims 2: Seasons|Seasons]]'' is installed. ===The Sims 3=== [[File:Thesims3-91-1-.jpg|thumb|Landgraab home in Sunset Valley.]] In ''The Sims 3'', the Landgraab family lives in a luxurious mansion at [[10 Summer Hill Court]], in [[Sunset Valley]]. Judging by the house and where they live, it is quite obvious that they are wealthy. It is the most expensive lot in town.
An elegant home on the most exclusive circle in town, this stately manor resounds with grandeur. Four fireplaces, a massive kitchen, formal and informal living areas, a large custom pool, two car garage, and elegant neoclassical landscaping round out its elegant features.

The Sims 3 (console) Landgraab's villa.png The Sims 3 (Console) Landgraab's villa backside.png ===The Sims 4=== {{Main|Acquisition Butte#Affluista Mansion}} [[File:TS4 Patch 174 2.png|thumb|Landgraab "Affluista Mansion" before / after patch 174.]] [Official lot's description required] {{expand}} {{clr}} ===The Sims 4: Castle Estate Kit=== [[File:The Grand Castle Estate.jpg|thumb|The Grand Castle Estate]] The Grand Castle Estate is a lot shared by Maxis in the gallery for the launch of "Castle Estate Kit". It's completely unfurnished.
This classic castle was once owned by the enchanting Princess Cordelia and is renowned as one of her numerous estates. It was later acquired by the notorious Landgraabs. Over the years, LandGraab Industries has preserved the exterior's timeless elegance but recently demolished the interior for unnamed reasons. Now they are looking for a lavish buyer ready to cover up… uh, I mean… adorn the inside of the castle to match the grandiose nature of the outside!
{{clr}} ===The Sims Freeplay=== [[File:The Sims Freeplay - The old Landgraab Estate.jpeg|thumb]] [[File:The Sims Freeplay - The old Landgraab Estate - interior.jpeg|thumb]] The old Landgraab Estate appears in the first chapter of The Sims Freeplay event "On the case: Heir of mystery".
The old Landgraab estate is elegant, opulent, and full of unanswered questions. From locked rooms to lingering glances, every corner hints at a story waiting to be uncovered. Across a series of live events, your Sims step into the role of investigator, piecing together clues and deciding who can truly be trusted.
{{clr}} ==Landgraab Chateau== [[File:Chateau_Landgraab.jpg|thumb|Chateau du Landgraab.]] In ''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures]]'', Sims can travel to [[Champs Les Sims]], home to a giant tomb known as the [[Chateau du Landgraab]]. Unlike most tombs, this tomb is rather unconventional in the sense that it is set in a huge mansion rather than an actual underground tomb. Most of the dungeon is actually above ground level. Since players also explore a basement underneath the chateau, it is one of the largest tombs in the game. Furthermore, it is very hard to get into, since its original inhabitant, [[Admiral Landgraab]], was very paranoid and filled his large estate with booby traps. To fully explore the house, players will need to fulfill several adventures in France that will give them keystones, and one keystone is only obtained by doing an adventure in China to explore the cellar area. It should also be noted that Pangu's Axe is required to explore a small underground part behind the house, near the groundskeeper's shack. Those who hope to complete the tomb should keep in mind that it is impossible to complete in one trip and may take (depending on Visa level) multiple trips to round out the exploration of the chateau. ==Trivia== *The Admiral's surname, Landgraab, was changed to Landgraaf in the Dutch translation of the game. He is named after the city of Landgraaf in the Netherlands. The name "Landgraaf" literally translates to "Land's Duke". *Japanese, Chinese (simplified), Chinese (traditional), Thai, and Korean refer to all members in [[The Sims 2: Open for Business|''Open for Business'']] as the fourth. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Landgraabs}} [[es:Familia Del Solar]] [[fr:Famille Plènozas]] [[it:Famiglia Landgraab]] [[nl:Landgraaf familie]] [[pl:Rodzina Landgraab]] [[pt-br:Família Quero-Tudo-Que-É-Seu]] [[ru:Семья Ландграаб]] [[Category:Families with 5 generations]] [[Category:Upper class families]] [[Category:Families with staff]]

'''Mimi Landgraab'''{{Vgversion|TS4}} (or '''Mimi Landgrabb'''{{Vgversion|TSC}}{{Vgversion|BO}}) is the daughter of [[Malcolm Landgraab|Malcolm]], the former step-daughter of [[Mom Landgraab|Mom]], and the sister of [[Dudley Landgraab|Dudley]]. She is a member of the wealthy [[Landgraab]] family and appears in ''[[The Sims (console)|The Sims]]'' for console and ''[[The Sims Bustin' Out (console)|The Sims Bustin' Out]]'' for console.

==The Sims (console)==
Mimi first shows up at the beginning of [[Reality Bites]] if the player's [[Sim]] is female. She allows the player's Sim to live in her old house for free, but they must clean and repair the house because Mimi and her friends trashed it while partying. After the player completes that level, Mimi will invite the player's Sim to be her roommate at the [[Party Animals]] house.

Unlike many other Sims in the game, Mimi is unwilling to skill-build, change careers, clean up, cook meals using the fridge, or answer the phone. However, she is willing to eat snacks, grill, and go to work.

Mimi usually gets promoted after going to work for the first time. Once promoted, the player can build 2 [[body]] [[skill]] points for her to be promoted again. After that, she will not get promoted to the next level.

Like Dudley, Mimi knows all the members of the [[Roomies household (console)|Roomies household]]. Strangely, she doesn't know the other members of the [[Landgraab family]], as they don't appear in her relationship panel.

Mimi also appears at [[The Party Motel]] multiplayer level with her brother, [[Dudley Landgraab|Dudley]], and members of the [[Roomies household (console)|Roomies]], [[Party Girls household|Party Girls]], and [[Party Guys household|Party Guys]] households.

==The Sims Bustin' Out ==
Choosing either the [[Movie Star]], [[Fashion Victim]], or [[Counter Culture]] career leads to the player moving in with Mimi. Sims are able to live in [[Mimi's Place]] until they have received two promotions in their [[career]] track. Although Mimi's house appears friendly, cheery, and girly, she is rather rude due to her personality, and if the player moves in with her, she will swear at them.

Upon moving into Mimi's Place for the first time, Malcolm will chastise Mimi for her shopaholic ways, repossessing her [[stove]] and [[Bar (object)#The Sims Bustin' Out (console)|bar]]. After the theft, Mimi will ask the player to retrieve her possessions. While the player is living with her, she will often leave during the day to go partying.

Mimi's signature social interaction is to brag about money.
==The Sims 4==
Mimi reappears along with her father, brother, and stepmother in an official recreation uploaded to the gallery by Maxis. Her clothing is a mix of both games she has appeared in.<ref>[https://www.ea.com/games/the-sims/the-sims-4/gallery/item/q5Scv32fEemG2Sap4Tf15w The Landgraab Family by Maxis]</ref>

==Biography==
As of [[The Sims 4/Patch 193|patch 193]], Queen Cordelia reappears in ''[[The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy]]'' as an ancestral [[Sim]] for the [[Thebe family|Thebe]] and [[Capp family|Capp]] [[Dynasty|dynasties]], a type of Sim that cannot be found in the game itself, only in [[family tree]]s, and whose information is stored in the game files.<ref>Cordelia Thebe's entry is the instance "C64F155592BC7810" in the SimulationFullBuild0.package file in the EP21 folder.</ref> She was the Queen of [[Ondarion]] prior to her [[death|passing]].

Cordelia has the sweet [[voice]] type and a [[Fears|fear of the dark]].

===Backstory===
Cordelia is said to be a member of the Royal House Thebe, who lost her home in a terrible giant sloth invasion, survived a [[kraken]] attack, and used its power for her own purposes. As a [[child]], she was a world-renowned [[Marbles|marble]] champion, winning one marble while playing with a [[mermaid]] in the tide pools near her home.

She had a great love for jazz music and even had her own band, which featured a saxophone player named Jacob Goldentips, a [[bass]] player named Martin Maxwell, as well as two unnamed members (trumpet and [[piano]]), which she later discovered to be the Prince of [[Willow Creek]], Edward Terrance Bertrand, in disguise. The piano also happens to be Cordelia's favorite instrument.

She adored tea, and princes would come from across the lands to have tea with her, but she much preferred the company of pirate captains and would end up dating a total of three pirate captains throughout her life. 

Cordelia loved the ocean and would quite often be found spending her free time at the [[beach]], lounging by tide pools for hours. She enjoyed watching the delicate sea anemones in the waters and was amused by the way crabs would hastily scuttle away from gulls that circled in the skies above. She liked the taste of crab, but her favorite meal was scallops fried in garlic, which was first cooked for her aboard her private submersible by her first pirate boyfriend's chef.

Living in a palace, Cordelia had many staff to cater to her every need, from [[maid]]s to [[gardener]]s, and even her own furniture artisans and astronomers. Two notable members of her staff are her butler, [[Bob The Butler|Bob]], and her personal chef, [[Matilda The Cook|Matilda]]. Looks were important to Cordelia, and she would usually be seen wandering the palace grounds dressed in a bustle and corset with her hair up and embellished with a jeweled headdress.

===Cordelia's Palace===
[[File:Princess Cordelia's Enlarged AI Resize.jpg|left|thumb|487x487px|Cordelia's painting titled ''Land-Coral Garden'' shows a coastal town]]
Princess Cordelia lived in a grand palace that was on the coast of a vast kingdom. It is not mentioned where this kingdom is located; however, one of Cordelia's paintings of her painting studio shows a view of seaside buildings, so the kingdom may be located near the coast. It is mentioned that residents of the kingdom dressed quite formally, with the women wearing long dresses and the men wearing top hats. Cordelia mentions that there are a lot of [[cat]]s living throughout the kingdom, and she dislikes them because they make her sneeze. 

The royal house was adorned with vases of beautiful flowers, and Cordelia enjoyed painting pictures of them. She also loved the fragrant smells that they released, filling the halls of the palace.

Cordelia was well educated, and she had hundreds of books in the palace library. She also had her own painting studio filled with her many paintings and sculptures, and she even had her own private submersible, The Epsilon.

===The Great Sloth Invasion===
[[File:BobTheButterStatue Transparent.png|thumb|283x283px|Statue of Bob the Butler]]
The Great Sloth Invasion was a disaster that struck Cordelia's kingdom and forced its residents to evacuate those who did not perish due to the invading Giant Sloths. Cordelia was able to escape in time and took everything she could carry into her submersible along with her pirate boyfriend, Captain [[Long John Buttercups]] and his crew, and a handful of her own staff from the palace, including her furniture artisans. Despite having 48 rooms, The Epsilon quickly became full, and unfortunately, there was no room for her beloved jazz band, or her butler and personal chef. So with a heavy heart, she had to fire them. In memory, she painted a series of silhouettes of her jazz band and various other entertainers that were left behind, and had a sculpture of her [[butler]] made. The princess would go on to stay in a cottage in [[Henford-on-Bagley]].

===Henford-on-Bagley {{Vgversion|TS4:CoL}}===
[[File:Princess Cordelia's Peasants Stairs.png|thumb|200px|right|Peasants stairs]]
One of the first locations she settled in was [[Henford-on-Bagley]]. She spent a lot of time enjoying the countryside and a simpler way of life. It has been speculated that she spent her time at a cottage at the very top of [[the Bramblewood]]. She would have most likely wandered the world and swam in the River Bagley as well. Since she left most of her staff behind, she was also missing her stair butler who used to carry her on the stairs, so she had to climb them herself. As mentioned in her diary, she called them "Peasants stairs". The waterfalls in Henford-on-Bagley, known as '''Cordelia Falls''', share her namesake.

===Pirate Boyfriends===
Being a princess, Cordelia was regularly in the company of various princes, but she was much more interested in pirates. Throughout her life, she dated three pirate captains. The first was Captain [[Long John Buttercups]], but things did not work out with him as he was a little too fond of Cordelia's corset and was disgustingly unhygienic, even after Cordelia designed him a sink. Cordelia then met the handsome and well-groomed, yet unbearably vain Captain [[Chaz MacFreeling]], but she quickly tired of his narcissism (and obsessive mirror-looking) and broke things off with him. Her third boyfriend was the clumsy Captain [[Rodrigo De Pablo]], who was said to possibly be the greatest love of her life. He was always getting himself hurt whilst aboard The Epsilon, including burning his feet. Cordelia gave him a peg leg for this, but one time when they were sitting together by a fire, his peg leg caught on fire. On Cordelia's ottoman, it states, "At least he never suffered a broken heart." This means it is possible Rodrigo was killed in this incident, further supported by [[Camille Soto]]'s response through the ''Gravevine Gossip'' interaction. However, she also states people say Cordelia hired a witch to trap him in a glass bottle that she cast out to sea due to his apparent [[romantic (social type)|love]] [[affair]] with [[List of minor Sims#T|Lady Tartosa]]. Some also say he [[death|died]] choking on a tart, which Camille believes to be the least ridiculous explanation. His death would have been tragic for Cordelia, as he was said to be the greatest love of her life.

All three of Cordelia's pirate boyfriends had beloved parrots, and each captain had a plate crafted to commemorate their parrot. However, each time Cordelia broke up with the pirates, she was left stuck with the plate and soon had quite the collection. The item has a fourth plate for Cordelia's fourth boyfriend, who is referred to as JWBB in a carving from the Beard Beard Cave in Tomarang.{{Vgversion|TS4:FR}} This man is John Wilson a.k.a. Beard Beard the Pirate, author of the goal book, ''The Log of the Final Voyage of Beard Beard the Pirate,'' which can be found upon arriving on the second island in ''[[The Sims 2: Castaway]]''.

===Life on The Eppsilon===
Princess Cordelia loved the outdoors, so life on a submersible must have been difficult. She spent a lot of her time in her workshop designing pieces of furniture inspired by her experiences of the sea for her furniture artisans to craft, most of which were drawn from elements of ocean life and from creatures she saw through the submersible's windows. She also enjoyed sitting at her desk and dreamily writing about her pirate boyfriends in her journal. Cordelia wanted to know what time it was outside, so she designed a clock, but as she still didn't know if it was day or night, she fed it to a [[kraken]] that regularly attacked her ship with [[fire]]. She actually used the kraken's fire to fire a porcelain bathtub that she designed.

Cordelia travelled the world in her submersible, selling the furniture she created at the port they were docked at, and to determine where The Eppsilon was going to travel next, Cordelia would spin the globe in her room, and wherever it landed, she would tell her pilot to take her there. Cordelia loved the winter and would ask her pilot to bring the submersible to the surface so she could watch the cold water dripping from the icicles frozen to the hull.

===Sulani {{Vgversion|TS4:IL}}===
Princess Cordelia and Rodrigo De Pablo spent some time in [[Sulani]], where they faced off against [[List of minor Sims#M|Dread Pirate Morgan]]. 

Below are three aspects of their story found in the Buried Treasure collection from ''[[The Sims 4: Island Living|Island Living]]''. 

=====The Fingers of Sulani Buried Treasure=====
Princess Cordelia the Bold pondered her gift. Upon disembarking, a young islander girl ran to her with colored stones and a wicker brush. Now staring out a hut window across [[Lani St. Taz]] waters to the Sulani volcano beyond, she traced the wicker lines then finally ran it through her long hair. "Not as elegant as carved ivory, but charming nonetheless."

"I say again, Morgan will break parley to betray you." Captain Rodrigo De Pablo sat, sharpening his sabre. "We are vulnerable. Let me bring the armada's forces ashore." His silhouette was imposing but his vision rarely reached beyond his weapon's range.

''Yes'', Cordelia thought, ''we are on the sword's edge, but how small the reward if we never up the ante. Dread Pirate Morgan has a ruthless reputation but is out-bluffed as Rodrigo if she's here only for the treasure hoard. The real treasure is the Sulani Islands themselves''.

"You ''will'' keep the armada as is; ''armed and ready'' for the parley at the sun's high peak."

Rodrigo snorted, and Cordelia traced the lava flow as she continued brushing her hair.

=====The Eyes of Sulani Buried Treasure=====
The Dread Pirate Morgan stood on a ledge that jutted dangerously past the volcano lip and over lava below. Sulfur burned her nostrils. "Fire is cleansing," she remarked.

The [[Mua Pel'am]] islander made no response, but the ex-first mate of [[List of minor Sims#H|Captain Handwich]] sniffed. "A hot bath in the wooden tubs here cleans just as well," he disdainfully countered.

Morgan clenched the Sulani Island coin that beckoned her from across the seas. She held it up and fire-light rippled across its face, a crashing wave. "The work is always dirty, and we've just started," Morgan admonished. With a Sulani crew member translating her intentions, finding an ambitious island faction was straightforward. Handwich's crew was even easier to turn; the fool starved his crew then crashed his ship. Above all, Cordelia was the danger with her armada in range of [[Ohan'ali Town]]. She'll block off immediate sea routes when the parley goes south, but ships cannot sail over land.

Morgan turned to give the volcano maw one last look and final taunt. "Your gaze lured me here, Sulani, so I return this to you. Tomorrow, I will have all of your eyes." She flipped the coin into the lava and watched as it was consumed.

=====Sulani Island Curator Plaque=====
With the treasure securely in the hold of The Red Annie, her captain, the Dread Pirate Morgan, sailed to oceans unknown to pursue the next grand plunder while behind her, the Ohan'ali Town port lay razed to the ground after the calamitous parlay with Princess Cordelia the Bold, her captain, Rodrigo De Pablo, and the hapless Captain Sam Handwich.

From the ashes, Ohan'ali Town was reborn as the prominent destination it is today, and the Mutiny of Ohan'ali became a significant page in the Sulani Islands' history.

===Tartosa {{Vgversion|TS4:MWS}}===
[[Tartosa]] is most likely one of the later locations Cordelia visited, as Camille states she did not arrive with her first partner but with someone else, presumably Rodrigo De Pablo. During her time in Tartosa, Cordelia developed a close relationship with Lady Tartosa. Camille believes they were unlikely lovers due to Cordelia's feelings towards Rodrigo. Still, Cordelia and Lady Tartosa spent a lot of time together at the beach, sailing and devouring tarts. Sadly, their relationship ended on rocky terms, but nobody knows why. Some believe it's because Lady Tartosa had an [[affair]] with Rodrigo. Others say that she stiffed Cordelia with a tart, which was a serious offense back then. 

During Cordelia's time in Tartosa, a local shipwright carved the likeness of Princess Cordelia and Rodrigo De Pablo into the figurehead of a ship. When the ship sank, those who remembered their love carried it to the top of the hill by Hideaway Falls as a reminder. A year passed, and it magically began to sprout leaves and branches, which was seen as a sign that their love lived on even though Rodrigo had passed. This tree came to be known as the Lover's Tree to the locals.

It is unknown why Cordelia left Tartosa; some say she was afraid of the sloth invasion coming to Tartosa, as they were known to be strong swimmers. Or that simply she was truly an adventurer at heart who could not stay in one place for too long. It could also possibly be the loss of her greatest [[romantic (social type)|love]], Rodrigo, that made her leave. However, it is known that after she left, she was one of the first [[Sim]]s to explore the arctic waters in her submersible, The Epsilon. It could also be presumed that during this time, she gave birth to a [[child]] known as [[Rodrigo Thebe]], the ancestor of [[Arnessa Thebe]], who remains in Tartosa with [[Laurent family|her family]].

===Ondarion {{Vgversion|TS4:R&L}}===
Princess Cordelia is revealed to be the original Princess Cordelia I and now has multiple descendants. One being [[Cordelia Thebe V|Cordelia V]], a legendary navigator. Like her ancestor, she is an intrepid seafaring socialite with a taste for lavish gatherings, amassed riches, and complicated affairs. Her other descendants in Ondarion include members of the [[Capp family]], siblings [[Juliette Monty|Juliette]] and [[Tybalt Capp|Tybalt]] and their children.

It is also revealed that Princess Cordelia I famously took not one, not two, but four pirate lovers. From two of these unions came children, a legacy that helped shape [[Verdemar]]'s cosmopolitan spirit. Later she [[marriage|married]] [[Eetion Thebe]] and had [[Andromache Thebe]], the mother of the late Grand Duke [[Consort Capp]].

==Biography==
Queen resided during her lifetime in [[Veronaville]], one of the [[neighborhood]]s shipped with ''[[The Sims 2]]''. She was the wife of [[Eetion Thebe|Eetion]], the mother of [[Andromache Thebe|Andromache]], the grandmother of [[Consort Capp]] {{Nee|Thebe|male}}, the great-grandmother of [[Goneril Capp|Goneril]], [[Regan Capp|Regan]], [[Kent Capp|Kent]], and the late [[Cordelia Capp]], and the great-great-grandmother of [[Juliette Monty|Juliette]], [[Hermia Capp|Hermia]], [[Tybalt Capp|Tybalt]], [[Miranda Capp|Miranda]], [[Hal Capp|Hal]], [[Desdemona Capp|Desdemona]], and [[Ariel Capp]].

Queen, like [[Priam Albion]], her daughter, and her husband, can be added to the family for a brief second through the [[Tombstone of Life and Death]]. If the game is paused, and the player directs her to do something, the player can have her stay for a bit longer. But in order for Queen to reappear permanently, her "Death Token" must be removed through [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]]. According to her SimDNA in SimPE, her hair was red before it turned gray. According to her age data, she had 20 days left in the [[elder]] [[life stage]] when she [[death|died]].

Although Queen has [[memories]] of her husband, unlike most pre-made deceased [[Sim]]s from Veronaville, she doesn't have the memory of Andromache's birth. Her great-granddaughter Goneril has dominant and recessive genetics for red hair, though Queen is the only one of Goneril's ancestors who has genetics for red hair. Queen uses the 10th face template and a slightly customized 1st nose template.

|Ode to Jazz 4: "Feeling Blue"

But firing her beloved jazz band remained a regret so sharp, she painted a series of pictures to honor them. This wistful silhouette portrays one of her musicians still playing blues in the deep blue (purplish) sea.
|§640
|-
|Ode to Jazz 2: "Goldentips" 
|When '''Princess Cordelia''' was forced to flee her kingdom, she had to leave her beloved jazz band behind. This wistful silhouette portrays the sax legend Jacob Goldentips still playing in the depths of the sea, which was how the Princess liked to imagine him.  
|§640
|-
|Ode to Jazz 5: "Ivory"
|'''Princess Cordelia''' loved piano most of all. Though she had cut her jazz band adrift during her escape from her kingdom, she continued to ache for their music, and so found herself painting instruments. The piano keys in this tribute seem to arch up toward the light, almost as if lifted by the current. Apt, isn't it?
|§700
|-
|Ode to Jazz 6: "Ghost Quartet" 
|Some days, the thought of her long-lost jazz musicians was simply too much for '''Princess Cordelia''' to bear. She even went so far as to have new instruments made, but with no one to play them, all she could do was paint pictures of them.
|§790
|-
|Blue for the Blues Wall Painting
|When '''Princess Cordelia''' was forced to flee her kingdom, she simply couldn't fit her beloved musicians on the submersible. This colorful portrait is a tribute to her bass player Martin Maxwell, and somehow made her feel less blue.
|§940
|-
|Ode to Jazz Triptych Trio 
|One thing '''Princess Cordelia''' simply couldn't fit on her submersible was her beloved jazz band. She so missed their music that she painted a series of pictures to commemorate it. Framed in celebratory gold frames, this collection reunites three of her favorite musicians-may they play together in peace on your wall.
|§1,120
|-
|Jazz Cats: Whiskers of a Forgotten Past
|One thing the '''Princess''' was thrilled to leave back in her former kingdom was cats. They shed everywhere and made her sneeze! But nostalgia is a funny thing, and so the princess found herself painting them. As you can tell from this design, her portrayals were a touch romantic.
|§1,455
|-
|Ode to Jazz Wall Painting 2: "Goldentips" 
|in Gold When '''Princess Cordelia''' was forced to flee her kingdom, she had to leave her beloved jazz band behind. This wistful silhouette portrays the sax legend Jacob Goldentips still playing in the depths of the sea, which was how the Princess liked to imagine him. [Must be placed on at least a two-story wall.]
|§1,533
|-
|"Blooming Beauty" Wall Painting
|Of course, there were no flowers in '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s subaquatic life, but she had an acute memory of the vases and vases of them that once adorned the Royal House. Oh, the fragrance! Princess Cordelia couldn't replicate the scent of course, but her painting was quite lifelike.
|§3,370
|-
|Land-Coral Garden 
|'''Princess Cordelia''' painted this before gradually fleeing from the giant sloths. Photographs were not commonplace yet, so this painting was all she had to remind her of her old palace's painting studio. While sitting comfortably on her escape submarine, she changed the name from "Flower Still Life," to "Land-Coral Garden."
|§7,500
|-
|Captain Chaz MacFreeling Mirror 
|'''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s second pirate boyfriend was handsome and, relative to other pirates, had good hygiene! Things started off great, but the princess noticed him looking in the mirror all the time; so vain. She promptly sent him on his way, giving him a handful of citrus for any future scurvy outbreaks, and naming all her mirrors after him.
|§790
|-
|Captain Chaz MacFreeling Elegant Mirror 
|'''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s second pirate boyfriend was handsome and, relative to other pirates, had good hygiene! Things started off great, but the princess noticed him looking in the mirror all the time; so vain. She promptly sent him on his way, giving him a handful of citrus for any future scurvy outbreaks, and naming all her mirrors after him. 
|§260
|-
|Imprisoned Vanity Mirror 
|No matter how long the Princess called the Eppsilon home, it was nonetheless a submersible, and like all submersibles, it was made of cold, unforgiving metal. In her sadder moments-most often after dumping a pirate boyfriend-'''Princess Cordelia''' favored this hostile glass, which reminded her of her tragic fate. Sigh. 
|§375
|-
|Captain Chaz MacFreeling Porthole Mirror 
|'''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s second pirate boyfriend was handsome and, relative to other pirates, had good hygiene! Things started off great, but the princess noticed him looking in the mirror all the time; so vain. She promptly sent him on his way, giving him a handful of citrus for any future scurvy outbreaks, and naming all her mirrors after him. 
|§975
|-
|Captain Chaz MacFreeling's Galleon 
|Princess Cordelia's 2nd pirate boyfriend Captain Chaz MacFreeling, was as vain about his galleon as he was about his looks. He commissioned '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s staff to carve him a replica, but he spent so much time gazing at it, she had it smashed to bits. This is a replica of the replica, rebuilt in astonishing detail by contemporary artisans.
|§1,225
|-
|Princess Cordelia Royal Bust 
|Before the Great Sloth Invasion, '''Princess Cordelia''' was said to have brilliant prospects. Princes came from miles around just to have tea with her. Of course, we know today that the Princess had a thing for pirates, but we still created this stunning bust to remind us how she would have looked to prince and pirate alike.
|§1,400
|-
|Princess Cordelia Royal Rug 
|One advantage a submersible has over nearly any other sea vessel is that the floor stays completely dry. But that's not to say it's warm-not in the least. '''Princess Cordelia''' designed this beautiful and luxurious rug to keep her royal toes as toasty as can be when she rose from bed on the Eppsilon.
|§205
|-
|Goldora Dove Décor
|When you can't see the sky, you start to miss everything in it: the sun, moon, stars and birds, of course. Longing for the gentle doves that used to alight outside her window, '''Princess Cordelia''' sketched these doves to be crafted from bars of gold. The modern version has been cost-reduced and is made of Goldora instead.
|§780
|-
|Polly Wants a Plate Tree 
|'''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s pirate boyfriends were all quite fond of their parrots. Every time she acquired a new boyfriend, he commissioned a plate in his parrot's honor. After her final romance withered, the Princess was stuck with a pile of plates, so she put them in a golden tree and hung it on the galley wall.
|§2,100
|-
|Sea Star Hand Towel Ring 
|Stellar as an accompaniment to the Sea Star Bath Towel Holder or as a standalone accent for your guest bath, the Sea Star Hand Towel Ring was designed by '''Princess Cordelia''' to replicate a sea star's powerful grip. It can withstand any amount of tugging, even by untamed pirates.
|§165
|-
|Sea Star Bath Towel Holder 
|'''Princess Cordelia''' had mixed feelings about sea stars, but she did admire their stick-to-itiveness. These royal towel holders have unparalleled grip, and make a stellar addition to any head to loo.
|§170
|-
|Captain Rodrigo de Pablo Cask 
|'''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s 3rd pirate boyfriend, Captain Rodrigo De Pablo, suffered many injuries aboard the Eppsilon. Once, while fleeing a kraken, the hatch slammed shut on his feet, and he couldn't stand for weeks. The Princess designed this cask while nursing her sweetheart back to health. With it she could quench his bottomless thirst whilst he lay prone beneath it.
|§570
|-
|Royal Crabtree Tea Set
|'''Princess Cordelia''' adored crabs almost as much as she adored tea. Nothing was more delightful that seeing them dart about the tide pools in mortal fear of gulls! The Princess designed this tea set to capture the crab's alacrity. She was working on a version that actually scuttled off, but the plans blew away while she was sipping tea.
|§770
|-
|The Where Should I Go? Ball
|'''Princess Cordelia''' was a strong-willed woman. Aboard her submarine, The Eppsilon, she travelled the world, building furniture and stopping at ports to sell her wares. When feeling adventurous, she would spin the globe and say "Where should I go?" Where it stopped, she went. Bring this replica globe into your home. Adventure!
|§1,720
|-
|Sea Princess Dining Hutch
|Cups and saucers and chargers, oh my! This fully stocked dining hutch designed by '''Princess Cordelia''' is inspired by the very sea itself! The legs are modelled after the shape of an octopus tentacle and the top of the hutch is adorned with a seashell motif.
|§2,500 
|-
|Jellyfish Bell Table Lamp
|While her submarine was docked, '''Princess Cordelia''' enjoyed some fresh air on the deck. Looking down she saw the glow of millions of jelly fish. It was breathtaking. Inspired by that moment, she designed this lamp and brought the shape and glow of the jellyfish bell to you. Aren't you glad she didn't include tentacles?
|§175
|-
|Scallop Table Lamp
|'''Princess Cordelia''' tried scallops for the first time while aboard her submarine. Cooked in garlic, they were the most delicious thing she had ever eaten. She was thankful for the experience and in honor of the poor scallop that lost its life, she designed this lamp. So touching! 
|§235
|-
|Sea Star Table Lamp
|Sea stars occasionally stuck themselves to the portholes of the submersible, rather annoyingly blocking the light, not to mention the view. Determined not to let her irritation get the better of her, '''Princess Cordelia''' created a lamp that is a glorious tribute to the sea star-with squat, pointy legs that can actually regenerate when harmed.
|§340
|-
|Long John Buttercups Table Lamp 
|Whenever '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Submarine dove or rose, she enjoyed watching the lights briefly flicker. This particular lamp was named after Princess Cordelia's first pirate boyfriend, Captain Long John Buttercups. He always said this lamp reminded him of his old galleon.
|§425
|-
|Two Thousand Ounces of Gold Under the Sea
|Dating pirates did have perks for '''Princess Cordelia'''. Birthday presents were usually flashy and made of gold. Such was the case for this candelabra, made of two thousand ounces of gold. Now released for mass market, it's made of brass.
|§115
|-
|Long John Buttercups Floor Lamp 
|Whenever '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Submarine dove or rose, she enjoyed watching the lights briefly flicker. This particular lamp was named after Princess Cordelia's first pirate boyfriend, Captain Long John Buttercups. He always said this lamp reminded him of his old galleon.
|§180
|-
|Anemone Wall Sconce
|'''Princess Cordelia''' was known to lounge by a tide pool for hours, just watching the fragile beauty entrapped within. One of her favorite creatures was the anemone, its petal-like tentacles waving innocently as it waited to ensnare its lunch. With subtle curls and an organic, unassuming form, this elegant wall sconce was created in the anemone's honor.
|§95
|-
|Sea Glass Wall Sconce
|The glass of this wall sconce was once clear and crisp. A special machine on the Lady '''Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Submarine processes the glass and gives it this opaque, soft feel. The machine blasts the glass with sand, salt, and steam which weathers this sconce in the same way as natural sea glass.
|§110
|-
|Old Life Gas Lamp
|When '''Princess Cordelia''' designed this lamp, she was feeling nostalgic for the land she left behind. While sitting in the workshop on her submersible, the Eppsilon, she thought of the dimly-lit gas lights that lined the streets and the silhouettes of women in long dresses and men in top hats walking by. Sigh. 
|§125
|-
|Cast Iron Flood Light
|It can get dark under the sea, particularly when pirates keep toppling into your lamps. This cast iron wall sconce is nearly indestructible, especially when mounted above hat-level. It casts a light so intense that '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s 2nd pirate boyfriend was known to use it for tanning, until she dumped him for being so vain.
|§130 
|-
|Long John Buttercups Wall Sconce
|Whenever '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Submarine dove or rose, she enjoyed watching the lights briefly flicker. This particular lamp was named after Princess Cordelia's first pirate boyfriend, Captain Long John Buttercups. He always said this sconce reminded him of his old galleon.
|§140
|-
|Ice Droplet Sconce
|On a cold winter's day, '''Princess Cordelia''' would ask her pilot to bring the submarine up to the surface. She loved watching water droplets freezing so beautifully as they dripped from the Eppsilon's hull. To commemorate and recapture that moment, she designed this wall sconce.
|§215
|-
|Tunicate Wall Sconce
|If you can't live under the sea like '''Princess Cordelia''', bring the ocean life to you! The Tunicate Wall Sconce is modelled after one of the most beautiful types of sea sponges. It was Princess Cordelia's favorite sconce. She often parked her submarine outside a reef and just soaked in the sea life, metaphorically.
|§225
|-
|Long John Buttercups Chandelier
|Whenever '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s Submarine dove or rose, she enjoyed watching the chandeliers tilt. This particular chandelier was named after Princess Cordelia's first pirate boyfriend, Captain Long John Buttercups. He always said this chandelier reminded him of his old galleon.
|§140
|-
|Sea Captain's Clock
|It's easy to lose track of time on a submersible, so '''Princess Cordelia''' designed this clock to create some order in her days. Unfortunately, it was still impossible to tell day from night, so she gave up and fed it to a kraken. Today, land-dwelling collectors find it much more useful.
|§810 
|-
|Copperrrr and Otherrr Metal Stove Hall – Wall
|'''Princess Cordelia''' wanted to take her beloved chef, Matilda, aboard her submarine, but she was unwilling to leave her family behind. Luckily one of Cordelia's pirate boyfriends had an amazing cook aboard his galleon. While purely for decoration, this copper hood helped the new cook feel at home.
|§100
|-
|Copperrrr and Otherrr Metal Stove Hall – Ceiling 
|'''Princess Cordelia''' wanted to take her beloved chef, Matilda, aboard her submarine, but she was unwilling to leave her family behind. Luckily one of Cordelia's pirate boyfriends had an amazing cook aboard his galleon. While purely for decoration, this copper hood helped the new cook feel at home.
|§160
|-
|Close Quarters Range Hood 
|This stove hood was invented by '''Princess Cordelia''' to keep her submersible from filling with smoke. Of course, it required a pretty long vent when she was leagues under the sea, but the modern version comes with everything you need.
|§305 
|-
|Princess Cordelia Bookcase
|When '''Princess Cordelia''' fled to her submersible, she left most of her books behind. But she couldn't bear to look uneducated, and so she had this bookcase constructed. Despite its delicate crablike legs, it's actually built sturdily to withstand the occasional turbulence at sea.
|§2,790
|-
|Unmentionables Dresser
|'''Princess Cordelia''' enjoyed structured clothing. Often sporting a bustle and a corset, undergarments were everything to her! She needed a lot of space to store her unmentionables so she designed this bottomless dresser that allowed her to change outfits at will. Amazing!
|§900
|-
|Faux Pas Path Lamp{{Vgversion|TS4:RG}}
|Legend has it that when these path lamps were first introduced to the royal gardens, '''Princess Cordelia''' infamously stumbled and tripped over one.
|§65
|-
|Princess Cordelia's Peasant Stairs{{Vgversion|TS4:CLV}}
|After the Great Sloth Invasion, '''Princess Cordelia''' was forced to flee her palace with few belongings and take refuge in the country. One of the first places she settled was Henford-on-Bagley. She spent lots of time enjoying the countryside, and a simpler way of life. One such novel experience for her was the concept of going up and down stairs. In her palace, her family prided themselves on efficiency and so she always had a stair butler who carried her up and down stairs. Since she had to fire all of her staff during the Great Sloth Invasion, unfortunately the stair butler could not join her in Henford-on- Bagley. On the bright side, she experienced climbing this very set of stairs for the first time. She referred to them as "peasant stairs" and wrote about them in her diary. There's a first time for everything. And if you're in the market for a good stair-butler, hers is still looking for work.
|§8
|-
|Break a Leg Dance Floor(s){{Vgversion|TS4:GT}}
|The perfect place for you to bust out all the latest dance moves: The Cowplant Calypso, The '''Cordelia''' Shuffle, The Sixam Strut, the Bear Man Boogie, and many more. You'll be the toast of the evening.
|§250-450
|-
|Strong Post{{Vgversion|TS4:MWS}}
|From the outside it may look like a regular post, fit for holding any regular banners. But this post is special, this post is ''the'' post that can hold banners filled with love. Strong as anybody's first love, this post is made with solid wood reclaimed from many of the pirate ships that graced Tartosa. Legends say it was built mostly from the very ship that hosted one of '''Princess Cordelia'''<nowiki>'</nowiki>s loves so you know that if you use this post with your love banners, your love will be of legend.
|§100 
|-
|Cordelia's Bust{{Vgversion|TS4:CC}}
|Let your crafted necklaces dazzle against this linen bust modeled after '''Princess Cordelia''' herself. The craftsmanship of this stand is of the highest quality, and there is no better way to showcase your masterpieces.
|§110
|-
|The Artisan's Glass{{Vgversion|TS4:CC}}
|Crafted from glass forged by the breath of dragons and framed by gold dug from the deepest caves, this mirror will reflect the shine that not only comes from your physical beauty but your inner gut health. The Dawnstone of '''Cordelia''' that crowns this mirror gives the design a whimsical touch that will add sparkle to any room.
|§250
|}

==Trivia==
[[File:University of Britechester.png|thumb|Description of University of Britechester]]
*In build mode, lots of items of the "Queen Anne" style have information about Princess Cordelia.
*According to the description of [[University of Britechester]], Princess Cordelia helped design the buildings of the university during her years there.
*The first reference to the name Cordelia is from ''[[SimCity (series)|SimCity 3000]]'', where [[Malcolm Landgraab]] is referenced as owning a hacienda on the resort island of San Cordelia.
*The official Gallery upload of Cordelia has her wearing a hairstyle exclusive to [[The Sims 4: Luxury Party Stuff]]. If the pack is not installed, she will be bald when downloaded.

[[File:Gibbi Point World Icon.png|left|60px]]'''Gibbi Point'''<ref>''(/ˈɡɪbi pɔɪnt/ "GIB-bee Point")''</ref> is a [[world]] shipped with ''[[The Sims 4: Adventure Awaits]]''. The world is expansive and rich with lore for Sims to uncover. Players can find the [[Jellyfish Junction#Adventure Story Map|Adventure Story Map]] at [[Jellyfish Junction|Jellyfish Junction]] to learn about quests and dive deeper into Peculiar Plumbird's history. It is a getaway destination filled with activities and facilities for Sims of all ages, and each neighborhood features public playgrounds for children to enjoy and embrace their childhood. The world also hosts a number of festivals where Sims can meet other townies and discover even more about the region's unique heritage. The endangered Plumbird can occasionally be spotted wandering somewhere in the world, though sightings are extremely rare.

==Description==
Many, many years ago, before it was inhabited, a great wave rushed through Gibbi Point to create a lush and fertile landscape. It became home to Jellyfish, Glow Worms and Plumbirds; it’s also where the world’s largest geyser, unusual caves of crystal, and a bioluminescent bay were formed. But it was more than these unusual creatures and natural wonders that drew Sims from all over to Gibbi Point.

==Real-World Inspirations==
===Etymology===
*The name origin of Gibbi Point is unknown. However, it is possible to have [[Wikipedia:Aboriginal Australians|Aboriginal Australian]] root, in Australian Aboriginal languages like [[Wikipedia:Dharug language|Dharug]] and [[Wikipedia:Arabana language|Arabana]], the word "gibba" or "giba" means "stone" or "rock." Combined with the word "point," where refers to a narrow piece of land that extends into a body of water in geography. The name is likely named after [[Jellyfish Junction#Peninsula of Fletcher View|Fletcher View peninsula]] in Jellyfish Junction, where the Lonely Lighthouse stands.
*[[Wanderwood Wilds]] is simply comprised of "wander" and "wood," where "wander" refers to roaming or exploring, and "wood" means "forest" in British English. Combined with "wilds," it emphasized the untamed and natural landscape which the neighborhood is located in. The name can be translated to "a wild forest to be explored."
*[[Jellyfish Junction]] is named after the jellyfish, a popular delicacy in the world, combined with the word "junction" which refers to a place where two or more lands, roads, or waterways meet. The name may reference the network of jetties that connect the area with others in the town square. However, it could also be named after the neighborhood's cove, which borders the open sea beyond view.
*[[Crystal Valley]] is named after the crystals that appeared in the dried-up gold mines following an unusual occurrence long ago, according to world's lore. A "valley" refers to a low area of land between higher ground, and the name reflects its location settled down east of the mountain range in Gibbi Point.

===Settings & Cultural Influences===
*Gibbi Point is thought to be inspired by [[Wikipedia:Aotearoa|Aotearoa]] ([[Wikipedia:New Zealand|New Zealand]]). Additionally, it is also said to be inspired by [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australia]], and [[Wikipedia:List of national parks of the United States|national parks]] of the [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]].
*The landscape may be inspired by [[Wikipedia:Queenstown,_New_Zealand|Queenstown]], a popular resort town in [[Wikipedia:Otago|Otago]], New Zealand. It could also be inspired by the [[wikipedia:Gold Coast, Queensland|Gold Coast]] in Queensland, Australia, which is a coastal city with a hinterland full of rainforests, national parks and rockpools, which is also a popular tourist destination.
*The Plumbird of Gibbi Point heavily resembles the rare [[Wikipedia:Takahē|Takahē]] minus the green [[plumbob]]-like feather. The Takahē itself is a flightless bird, endemic to [[Wikipedia:South Island|Te Waipounamu]] (New Zealand's South Island).

In Wanderwood Wilds:
*The [[Wanderwood Wilds#Hothead Rock Geyser|Hothead Rock Geyser]] and hot springs with sulfur deposits resemble those found in [[Wikipedia:Rotorua|Rotorua]], New Zealand, as well as in [[Wikipedia:Yellowstone National Park|Yellowstone National Park]], [[Wikipedia:Wyoming|Wyoming]].

In Crystal Valley:
*The [[Crystal Valley#Electric Lagoon|Electric Lagoon]] with the glowworm backdrop resembles the [[Wikipedia:Waitomo Glowworm Cave|Waitomo Glowworm Cave]] in New Zealand. The cave is known for ''[[Wikipedia:Arachnocampa luminosa|arachnocampa luminosa]]'', a glowworm species of fungus gnat that is endemic to New Zealand.

==Trivia==
*The world features builds from five EA Creator Network members: [https://beacons.ai/jeyjeybink Jeyjeybink], [https://www.daniellebuilds.com/ daniellebuilds], [https://www.youtube.com/@gryphi Gryphi], [https://www.youtube.com/kiwisimskate KiwiSimsKate], and [https://www.instagram.com/axiisims axiisims].<ref>https://x.com/axiisims/status/1963634534517260641</ref> It is the eleventh world to have all lots built entirely by Simmers and the thirteenth world overall to contain lots built by Simmers.
*This is the third world to feature more than one 64x64 lot, following [[Windenburg]] and [[Ravenwood]], which came with ''[[The Sims 4: Get Together]]'' and ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death]]'', respectively.
*This is the second world in ''The Sims 4'' to feature waterfront lots, with the first being [[Sulani]].
*[[Skip Broke]] first appeared in ''[[The Sims 2]]'' as the late [[Ghost]] husband of [[Brandi Broke]] and dad of [[Dustin Broke|Dustin]] and [[Beau Broke]].
*[[Agora Tchotchke]] is originally from [[Four Corners]], one of the neighborhoods in the story mode of ''[[The Sims Life Stories]]'', where she acts as an antagonist in [[Riley's story]].
*There's a crashed plane in the Jellyfish Junction ocean that is similar to the disappearance of Amelia Earhart and her plane.

Sage.title: Sage
Sage.text:
'''Sage''' is a kind of [[Non-playable character|NPC]] introduced with ''[[The Sims 4: Realm of Magic]]''. They are a kind of [[spellcaster]] mentor that will help other Sims become spellcasters themselves, alternatively, they also make it possible to turn a spellcaster back into a normal Sim. They are found at HQ in [[The Magic Realm]] and are identified with a glowing colourful symbol of the school of magic in place where a plumbob would be. There are three different sages; the Sage of Mischief, the Sage of Untamed and the Sage of Practical Magic. They each have fully learned the school of magic they are a sage of, as well as all [[Alchemy#The Sims 4: Realm_of_Magic|alchemy]] recipes. They will teach spells of the school of their magic and alchemy recipes for the level of the spellcaster and the [[Spells (The Sims 4: Realm of Magic)|Ultimate Spell]] of their school of magic once a spellcaster is a [[Spellcaster#Spellcaster Ranks|Virtuoso spellcaster (rank 5)]]. However, to learn from the sages you will have to be at friend relationship level, and have a spell to learn for your rank. Otherwise, they will exclaim that you need to get to know them better. Note that if you have recently learned a spell from the sage the interaction will be greyed out for a period of time. They can also train spellcasters which is a social that includes the "practice magic" interaction, so you can increase relationship with the sage, earn spellcaster experience and if missing a spell up to your rank learn a spell. Potions are easier to learn from sages as the cooldown between asking somewhat short, making alchemy very easy to learn all the recipes. Also, if your spellcaster destroyed or is missing their Glimmerstone you can ask a sage for another one. The sages are all are Virtuoso spellcasters and each vary in perks, however, they are all [[Spellcaster#Perks|Master Duelist]]. This makes them somewhat difficult to defeat in dueling. Interestingly enough, they do not have [[Spellcaster#Magical bloodline|bloodline traits]]. If one of the sages would be added to a household they will lose their status as sage and will be replaced with a new one. ==Standard sages==

The '''Dragoste family''' is a pre-made family featured in the reveal trailer for ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death]]''. It consists of a single father, [[Papa Dragoste|Papa]], his three children, [[Angelika Dragoste|Angelika]], [[Travis Dragoste|Travis]], and [[Liv Dragoste|Liv]], Angelika's husband, [[Paul Dragoste|Paul]], and their two daughters, [[Justine Dragoste|Justine]] and [[Robin Dragoste|Robin]]. The family can be found in the [[Gallery]], where they were uploaded by [[Maxis]].<ref>[https://www.ea.com/games/the-sims/the-sims-4/gallery/item/KXMacIuGQ32W96ptWhGKDw Dragoste by Maxis]</ref>

==Biography==
While in the trailer, Papa was seen passing away in his sleep; he is still alive in the uploaded household, likely to give leeway for the player to play out their own [[Funeral]] for the elder. The mother of Liv, Angelika, and Travis is either out of the picture or has already passed away.

Travis and Angelika were shown arguing over their deceased father's will in the Reveal Trailer, suggesting they may not exactly get along well; this is not reflected in the actual game, having a mutual Friend relationship score. Perhaps it is meant to show they are meant to have a falling out in the future, once their father passes.

In fact, everyone in the family seems to get along very well, except for Paul, who has a good relationship with only his wife and kids, seeing his in-laws as mere acquaintances and vice versa.
